Keysight Technologies reported record results for the fiscal third quarter ended 2026-07-31, with revenue of 1.85 billion, up 36.54% from a year earlier, and net income of 397 million, up 107.85% [D1]. It was the second consecutive record quarter for the company, and management said the results exceeded the high end of the guidance range for both revenue and earnings per share [D1]. Gross margin was 65.9% and net margin was 21.5% [D1]. Communications Solutions Group revenue rose 43.09% to 1.35 billion and Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue rose 21.60% to 501 million [D1]. Management guided the fourth quarter to revenue of 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion, growth of 37% at the mid-point, and earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 on a diluted share count of about 172 million [D1]. Management attributed the quarter to the rapid scaling of the AI infrastructure ecosystem, with wireline orders more than doubling year over year and wireline revenue exceeding wireless for the first time [D3].

The argument in the market is whether this demand is durable or whether supply caps how much of it converts into revenue [D3]. Management said supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue and that the supply environment is less flexible than a year ago [D3]. Management also said revenue conversion is likely to be nonlinear over the next several quarters [D4]. The bulls point to the highest-ever monthly funnel intake in the most recent month and to a pipeline that keeps growing [D4]. On the other side, management warned that the one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 will not repeat and that this sets a high comparison bar [D3]. The mix of the wireline business has also shifted from research and development toward manufacturing as AI data centre build-outs scale, a change management flagged alongside the record quarter [D3].

The shares closed at 333.42, above the 20-day average of 330.47, the 50-day average of 326.21 and the 200-day average of 289.31, and the trend state reads uptrend [D1]. The valuation shows a forward price to earnings of 20.66 against a trailing price to earnings of 45.89 and trailing earnings per share of 7.38 [D1]. The sell side is more optimistic than that, though price targets of this kind are frequently set for reasons other than a genuine view of where the shares will trade [D5]. The balance sheet gives the position room, with total assets of 11.92 billion, stockholders' equity of 6.57 billion and net debt of 141 million [D1].

The plan is to stay with the position while the demand evidence holds and to require supply to loosen before adding to it [D3]. What confirms the view is delivery of fourth quarter revenue of 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion and earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 [D1]. What also matters is that Communications Solutions Group revenue holds at or above 1.35 billion, Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue holds at or above 501 million, and gross margin holds near 65.9% with net margin near 21.5% [D1]. The nearest dated items are management's participation in investor conferences on September 11, 2026 and September 15, 2026, which are the next scheduled occasions for the company to speak to the supply question [D6].
